//: Template gate configuration. Copy to your own repository, usually as
governance/gates.json, and replace everything below with your rules.
This file is a TEMPLATE. The configuration is layer 3 and belongs to the
adopter, never to the engine. The entries here illustrate the shape and
are not recommendations: pick your own conventions.
Every key must name a gate that exists, or the run fails. A typo would
otherwise leave you believing a rule is enforced while nothing runs.
Scope is regular expressions over repository-relative paths, not globs,
because a regex means exactly one thing everywhere.
Run: node <engine>/scripts/run-gates.mjs --staged --config governance/gates.json

forbidden-chars.//: Invisible characters that survive review because nobody can see them.

//: Indentation is the clearest illustration that this is a capability.
'^\t' means indent with spaces; '^ ' would mean indent with tabs.
Both are defensible, which is exactly why neither lives in the engine.

patterns.message: resolve or convert to a tracked issue before merge

required-patterns.//: Absence, which forbidden-patterns cannot express. include is mandatory here.

patterns.message: source files need a copyright header

//: Marks in code that cite a rule must name a rule that exists. Catches the
drift where a rule is superseded and the comment keeps claiming the link.
No register path here: the register has one home, given to the runner
with --register or $GOVERNANCE_REGISTER, and repeating it would give the
same fact two places to disagree. Set 'ids' instead if there is no
register at all.
Makes changing a crown-jewel file deliberate rather than incidental.
Needs a change set, so it only runs with --staged. Additions are never
blocked: a file that does not exist yet cannot be silently overwritten.
